quantities.label: Part type rule: a part is Compact when its uncompressed bytes < min_bytes_for_wide_part, its rows < min_rows_for_wide_part or its level < min_level_for_wide_part, else Wide. An insert measures the block in memory (Block::bytes); a merge sums the inputs' on-disk uncompressed column bytes, uses level max(input levels) + 1, and is Wide when any input is Wide. A mutation keeps the source type.

hint.sql: SELECT part_type, count(), sum(data_uncompressed_bytes) FROM system.parts WHERE active AND database = '<db>' AND table = '<table>' GROUP BY part_type

mapping.part_type: part_type of the active parts the rule produced

quantities.label: Upload sizing: WriteBufferFromS3 fills a first buffer of multipart_first_part_bytes; an object that fits it, even exactly, is one PutObject. A second buffer (multipart_next_part_bytes) starts the multipart upload; every multipart_growth_parts parts the part size grows by multipart_growth_factor (up to 5 GiB). The last part holds the remainder.

quantities.label: Async flush: inserts with the same query shape and settings share a buffer; it is flushed into one part per partition when its unparsed bytes reach async_insert_max_data_size, when async_insert_max_query_number inserts accumulate with deduplication on, or when its deadline passes. The deadline is the first insert time plus an adaptive timeout between async_insert_busy_timeout_min_ms and _max_ms that grows while inserts are frequent. With wait_for_async_insert = 1 a client waits for the flush, so only concurrent inserts share one.

quantities.label: Fetch vs local execution of a replicated merge: the replica merges locally unless always_fetch_merged_part is set, execute_merges_on_single_replica_time_threshold > 0 picks another replica (merges only; with zero-copy also remote_fs_execute_merges_on_single_replica_time_threshold), a source part is missing locally, or the entry is older than prefer_fetch_merged_part_time_threshold and its sources hold at least prefer_fetch_merged_part_size_threshold bytes on disk while a replica has the result. A mutation follows the same rule with always_fetch_mutated_part, without the single-replica branch, and keeps the source part type. A replica that already has the part or a covering one skips the entry.
